title: Committee of Supply – Head T (Ministry of National Development)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head T (Ministry of National Development)

sections.label: HDB estate age and budget cut
sections.summary: A motion seeks to reduce Head T's allocation by $100, noting Singapore's oldest HDB estate is about 61 years old.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I beg to move, "That the total sum to be allocated for Head T of the Estimates be reduced by $100".

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: The oldest HDB estate in Singapore today is about 61 years of age.

sections.label: Revamping Remaking Heartland Program
sections.summary: The Remaking Heartland Program should be revamped for business variety, hybrid shops, local brands and innovation, as many flats suffer spalling concrete.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: To better utilise them, the Remaking Heartland Program should be revamped.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: What is required is not simply remaking of physical infrastructures, but a renewal on business varieties, hybrid presence of shops, digital & physical, supporting our local brands and trades, and innovation launchpads right in our own heartland.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Despite all the efforts to maintain and upgrade them, many of these flats suffer from spalling concrete at their ceiling and at the kitchen.

sections.label: Periodic Facade Inspection and cost sharing
sections.summary: BCA will require Periodic Facade Inspection for buildings above 20 years and 13 metres from the second quarter, with HDB co-sharing costs with Town Councils.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Additionally, it was mentioned that to address building facade issues, BCA will make it a requirement for building owner to perform a Periodic Facade Inspection (PFI) for all buildings above 20 years and above 13 metres in height commencing from second quarter of this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As the Town Council chairperson, I am thankful that HDB is co-sharing with Town Councils the costs for Periodic Facade Inspection as well as repair works.

sections.label: HDB programmes and Lift Upgrading Programme
sections.summary: HDB rolled out NRP, ROH and CUP, and the Minister said 150 blocks are not eligible for LUP, with no need to inform residents directly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Hence, we should strive to adopt best practices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I believe this is HDB's fundamental consideration when they rolled out national programmes such as Neighbourhood Renewal Programme (NRP), Remaking Our Heartland Programme (ROH) and Carpark Upgrading Programme (CUP) in rejuvenating and refurbishing our ageing public housing estates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: Last month, the Minister for National Development replied to my Parliamentary Question (PQ), informing me that there are 150 HDB blocks which are not eligible for the Lift Upgrading Programme (LUP), blocks where there are still residents who do not have same floor access to lifts, that there is no need to inform residents in affected blocks directly that no LUP is available for now, as HDB will continue to explore new technical methods to bring down LUP costs, and to improve accessibility without direct lift access.

sections.label: Residents asking for HDB costing
sections.summary: Some residents asked HDB to share the costing involved and how much each resident must pay, so they can decide if they can afford it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: For blocks where cost is the issue, some of my residents have asked that HDB should share with residents the costing involved, and how much each resident must pay, so that residents have a better understanding of the situation including deciding for themselves whether this is something they can afford and are willing to pay for.

sections.label: Dedicated lanes for foot, bicycles, PMD
sections.summary: The speaker supports separate dedicated lanes for those on foot, bicycles and PMD, and expects e-scooters may return to PCN in greater numbers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: In the interest of safety, I am in support of having separate dedicated lanes for those on foot, for bicycles and PMD.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: Once the extended cycling network is up, we may see the return of the e-scooters to our PCN in greater numbers.

sections.label: PPHS rental demand and BTO supply
sections.summary: PPHS rental demand rose above 12 times available supply in February, and BTO supply in 2020 was increased to about 16,700 flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: One indicator is the demand for rental units under the Parenthood Provisional Housing Scheme (PPHS), which has risen to more than 12 times the available supply in February.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Minister Desmond Lee replied in Parliament in October 2020 that the BTO flat supply in 2020 was increased to about 16,700 flats to meet demand.

sections.label: PSP proposal for rental HDB flats
sections.summary: With 7% of housing supply vacant, PSP favours permanent rental HDB flats and recommended small short-term rental flats of up to five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: According to property market statistics, there are 7% vacant units in the whole housing supply in the country.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: While not an immediate solution, the Progress Singapore Party is in favour of making rental HDB flats a permanent choice in the long term.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We had recommended the provision of small but good-quality rental flats for short-term occupation of up to five years as an additional housing option for young Singaporean families and to act as a buffer to absorb sudden surge in excess demand, so as to smooth out the property price cycle.

sections.label: Commercial use of carpark top floors
sections.summary: The speaker asks HDB to consider designating topmost floors of HDB-owned multi-storey carparks for expanded commercial use.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Needless to say, this represents an inefficient utilisation of our built environment.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I would like that HDB consider the possibility of designating in part or whole the topmost floors of HDB-owned multi-storey carparks for expanded commercial use.

sections.label: Converting under-utilised MSCP space
sections.summary: There is no systematic scheme to convert under-utilised MSCP space into commercial uses such as cafes, bubble tea shops or central kitchens.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: As far as I am aware, however, there is no systematic scheme to permit the conversion of under-utilised MSCP space into other commercials uses, such as cafés or bubble tea shops or central kitchens.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Enabling such use would not only provide additional hubs for residents to shop, eat and socialise.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It would also offer convenient employment opportunities for locals who may wish to work for such businesses.

sections.label: WFH and HDB estate design
sections.summary: The issue concerns business district space design and physical infrastructure in housing estates, given WFH may become permanent, requiring broadband investment and childcare and eldercare roles.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For MND, the issue to be raised here concerns the design of use of space in the business district, not just the central business district, and possible physical infrastructural support in housing estates to take account of the likelihood that even after COVID-19, as well as during a possibly long-drawn pandemic, WFH arrangements in some form might become a permanent fixture of working life.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, with more people working from home, there might be a need for bigger digital infrastructure investment to strengthen broadband services for people working from home.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With WFH becoming a permanent fixture of working arrangement for many employees, HDB estates can be organised to support two additional important roles of workers who have children or elderly parents: providing childcare and providing eldercare.

sections.label: Fewer workers and office space
sections.summary: With fewer workers travelling into the business district, there may be implications for rents and use of office space.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Second, with fewer workers travelling into the business district, there may be implication for rents as well as use of office space.

sections.label: Lifecycle carbon emission guidelines
sections.summary: MND is asked to consider internal guidelines estimating lifecycle carbon emissions for greenfield and brownfield developments to guide trade-offs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
sentences.text: Will MND consider developing internal guidelines to estimate lifecycle carbon emission for both greenfield and brownfield developments so that the Government can make the right carbon emission trade-offs on this decision which may shape the eventual decision on whether to go greenfield versus brownfield?

sections.label: Project update request
sections.summary: MND is asked whether it can provide an update on the project at this juncture.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
sentences.text: At this juncture, can MND provide an update on the project?

sections.label: Change of use TDL undertaking
sections.summary: URA is asked whether it could require change of use applications to include an undertaking that the TDL was discussed between landlord and tenant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Could URA require that all change of use applications include an undertaking from the applicant that the TDL has been discussed between the landlord and tenant.

sections.label: TDL rebates or deferments
sections.summary: URA is asked whether it can consider giving businesses rebates or deferments of their TDL.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Can URA consider giving such businesses rebates or deferments of their TDL?

sections.label: Built To Rent housing
sections.summary: Built To Rent, or multi-family, is private rental housing owned and managed by institutional landlords and is becoming more prevalent in other capital cities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A kind of housing that is becoming more prevalent in many other capital cities is Built To Rent (BTR), otherwise known as multi-family.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: These private rental developments are owned and managed by institutional landlords.

sections.label: BTR institutional investor capital
sections.summary: The BTR sector is an asset class sought after by global institutional investors, with private global capital ready to be tapped.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The BTR sector, for example, is an asset class sought after by many global institutional investors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In the BTR sector I mentioned earlier, the private global capital is ready to be tapped in this instance.

sections.label: Master Plan 2019 schemes
sections.summary: The schemes ran from 27 March 2019 for five years from gazette for Master Plan 2019, and asks how many developments met their conditions two years on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: The schemes were implemented from 27 March 2019 for a period of five years from the date of gazette for Master Plan 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: Two years after they were introduced, how many developments have fulfilled the conditions of these schemes?

sections.label: PPHS applications oversubscription
sections.summary: On 24 February PPHS applications exceeded available flats by 13.5 times, and March was two times oversubscribed two days in.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: Chairman, when I last checked on 24 February, PPHS applications have exceeded the number of flats available by 13.5 times.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: I believe this oversubscription is not unique to February alone with the PPHS for March two times oversubscribed despite being just two days into the month.

sections.label: Homeless public rental tenants
sections.summary: A survey a year ago found 15% of homeless interviewed were registered tenants in public rental flats who left over problems with co-tenants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
sentences.text: There may also be occasions when one of the occupants may just then shift out and sleep in the void deck.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
sentences.text: There was a survey done a year ago, where 15% of the homeless interviewed say that they are a registered tenant in a public rental flat, but they had problems getting along with their co-tenant, and hence, they moved out and lived in the void deck.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
sentences.text: We should always encourage families to stay together; but on a case-by-case basis, allow singles to rent a 1-room flat.

sections.label: Larger rental flats for families
sections.summary: With only one bedroom, parents and children sleep in the living room, so HDB is urged to allow larger rental flats for larger families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
sentences.text: So there will be only one bedroom for the parents and the children, whether it is three or four of them, they would all have to sleep in the living room.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
sentences.text: So I urge that HDB to review the policy of only having 1- to 2-room rental flats and allow larger rental flats for families which are larger.

sections.label: Neighbour noise and smoke complaints
sections.summary: Over past months the speaker received more complaints about neighbour noise, smokers' smoke drifting into flats, and pigeons and cat droppings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
sentences.text: Over the past months, I have received more complaints from residents about noise from their neighbours, about smokers who smoke outside their windows and the smoke drifts into their flat, about pigeons and cat droppings.

sections.label: Health of rental housing residents
sections.summary: A 2018 study found public rental housing associated with poorer health, and another found such patients more likely to have heart disease and hospital re-admission.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: In 2018, there was a study done to examine the healthcare utilisation of the low-income community in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: It found that staying in public rental housing was associated with poorer health outcomes and health status.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: Another study found that patients living in rental housing were more likely to have heart disease commonly associated with stress, were more likely to use anti-depressant medication, staying in hospitals longer than other income groups and more frequently re-admitted into hospital.

sections.label: Waiving public housing rental fees
sections.summary: The speaker links stress to ill health and bills, and urges MND to waive rental fees for public housing residents for six months to a year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: High stress leads to more ill health which leads to more medical bills and more stress.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: I urge MND to waive the rental fees of all public housing residents for a minimum of six months to a year.

sections.label: Mutual rental programme opt-in pilot
sections.summary: The speaker urges MND to consider the mutual rental programme as opt-in and to pilot it with willing elderly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: (In English): I urge MND to consider this mutual rental programme as an opt-in programme and to pilot with elderly who are willing.

sections.label: Joint Singles Scheme flat mate difficulties
sections.summary: The Joint Singles Scheme requires a single tenant to rent a flat with a flat mate, which can cause difficulties if they do not get along.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
sentences.text: The Joint Singles Scheme, which requires a single tenant to rent a flat together with a flat mate, can lead to difficulties if the flat mates do not get along.

sections.label: Larger flats for larger families
sections.summary: The speaker requests that MND and HDB consider supporting larger families in public rental housing by providing larger flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
sentences.text: Chairman, I would like to request if MND and HDB would consider supporting larger families in public rental housing by providing larger flats?

sections.label: Bigger rental units for families
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether there are options for bigger rental units for families with four members or more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
sentences.text: Are there options for bigger rental units for families with four members or more?

sections.label: Reviewing JSS renting alone criteria
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether MND can review the JSS and consider publishing specific criteria under which a person can rent a flat alone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can MND review the JSS and consider publishing a set of specific criteria under which a person can rent a flat alone?

sections.label: EIP restricts HDB buyer pool
sections.summary: The EIP restricts the pool of potential buyers and sellers of HDB flats for minorities, potentially creating artificial inequalities or negative externalities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The problem with the EIP is that it restricts the pool of potential buyers and sellers of HDB flats for minorities, potentially creates artificial inequalities or negative externalities in the medium to long run.

sections.label: Help for EIP-affected flat owners
sections.summary: MND is asked whether it would consider a discount on the next purchase and an EIP price harmonisation grant for these flat owners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Besides the case-by-case basis now via time extensions, would MND consider helping these flat owners by providing a discount on their next purchase and EIP price harmonisation grant to potentially reduce an indirect negative market effects of the EIP?

sections.label: Community Care Apartments housing
sections.summary: HDB introduced public housing types such as Community Care Apartments, with prices from $52,000, variable leases and care options.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: To meet the diverse housing needs of our population, including first-timer families, seniors and singles, the HDB has also introduced innovative types of public housing such as the Community Care Apartments which other hon Members have spoken about.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: These flats can start from prices as low as $52,000 and have variable leases and even come with advanced care options such as housekeeping.

sections.label: Rise in social disamenity feedback
sections.summary: Reports of feedback on social disamenities rose from 280 per month to about 2,100 per month in April to June 2020.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As a result, there was an increase in reports of feedback on social disamenities from 280 per month to about 2,100 per month in April to June 2020.

sections.label: Tampines design themes and features
sections.summary: Residents choose options only when personally satisfied with designs, and completed Tampines design themes drew outside attention.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
sentences.text: Only when personally satisfied with the designs, do we offer the options for residents to choose from.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
sentences.text: We even give names to the design themes and I am happy that so far, we have completed the #TampinesTVscreen and #TampinesTudor series, and we are in the process of painting the #TampinesTingkat and #TampinesKuehlapis designs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
sentences.text: The Tampines TV Screen has even inspired UNIQLO's 2019 National Day neighbourhood t-shirt design for Tampines, and more recently the TV Screen block façade was featured in Disney+'s promotional video.

sections.label: Voting function for OneService app
sections.summary: Given the OneService app's popularity, the speaker hopes MSO could look at providing a voting or straw poll function.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
sentences.text: Given the popularity of OneService app, I hope that the MSO could look at providing a voting or straw poll function.

sections.label: Platform for resident surveys
sections.summary: MSO is asked to consider developing a survey platform for Town Councils and grassroots organisations to reach residents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
sentences.text: However, local organisations like Grassroots and Town Council would not have the critical mass or scale to develop a robust platform for such surveys.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
sentences.text: So, I hope that MSO could consider developing one and offer the platform for the Town Council or organisations to reach out to residents so that we can promote greater community ownership and good neighbourliness.

sections.label: Pandemic impact on municipal services
sections.summary: The Minister is asked how municipal service delivery was affected during the pandemic and how agencies addressed challenges.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Can Minister share during the pandemic, to what extent were the delivery of municipal services affected, what were the challenges the Government agencies faced, and how did the agencies address these challenges to maintain the municipal service standards in Singapore?

sections.label: Closing the loop on matters
sections.summary: It asks how closing the loop on matters raised can be better managed going forward.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: How can closing the loop on such matters raised be better managed moving forward?

sections.label: MSO service improvements update
sections.summary: MSO is asked for an update on improvements made and other technology-enabled services residents can expect.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Can MSO provide an update on the improvements that have been made and what other technology-enabled service and improvements can residents look forward to?

sections.label: App as neighbourhood platform
sections.summary: It asks whether the app can be a one-stop neighbourhood platform to connect residents and pull social support resources.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Given the strong calls for strengthening kampung spirit in the community, can the app be used as a one-stop neighbourhood platform to connect the community, enable residents' participation and pull resources from a social support angle?

sections.label: Reorganising the built sector
sections.summary: It states an urgent need to reorganise the built sector facing simultaneous challenges including demand, labour, productivity, green standards and a downturn.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Chairman Sir, can I take my cuts together?

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
sentences.text: There is an urgent need to reorganise the entire built sector which is facing a large number of simultaneous challenges, namely: the changing nature of demand of the built sector in the post-COVID-19 world; uncertainty in future source availability and cost of both skilled and unskilled foreign workers in the sector; the challenge of encouraging Singaporeans to come into the sector even as more jobs in the construction sector are more skill-based and working conditions have improved; the need to drive productivity through prefab, digitisation and capital intensive technology; the need to rebuild and remake our buildings not just new, but also current buildings to factor in new green standards; and last of all coping of the current industry cyclical downturn.

sections.label: Buildings carbon emissions share
sections.summary: Buildings account for over 20% of Singapore's carbon emission.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
sentences.text: Buildings account for over 20% of Singapore's carbon emission.

sections.label: Singapore Green Building Masterplan co-creation
sections.summary: The Government announced at COS 2020 that stakeholders will be invited to co-create the next Singapore Green Building Masterplan.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
sentences.text: The Government announced or at COS 2020 that various stakeholders will be invited to co-create the next edition of the Singapore Green Building Masterplan.

sections.label: Green Masterplan progress query
sections.summary: The speaker asks MND to share the progress made on the Green Masterplan.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
sentences.text: As such, can I get MND to share on the progress made on the Green Masterplan?

sections.label: Construction sector support measures
sections.summary: The Government introduced support measures including the Construction Support Package, Job Support Scheme and extensions to help the sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: The Government has stepped forward decisively to help the sector tide over with support measures such as the Construction Support Package, which co-funds additional costs that construction companies have to incur to put in place safety measures, as well as the Job Support Scheme and its various extensions to help businesses in the sector defray salary costs for Singaporeans and protect jobs and capabilities in the sector.

sections.label: DFMA adoption rate targets
sections.summary: In 2019 the sector achieved 31% DFMA adoption by gross floor area, and BCA aims to raise PPVC and APCS adoption to up to 70% by 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: In 2019, the sector achieved a 31% DFMA adoption rate in terms of gross floor area.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: In particular, for prefabricated prefinished volumetric construction, or PPVC, and advanced precast concrete system, or APCS technologies, BCA is looking to raise the adoption rate to up to 70% by 2025.

sections.label: BCA Green Mark certification progress
sections.summary: To-date, more than 40% of buildings have been greened under the BCA Green Mark certification scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: To-date, more than 40% of our buildings have been greened under the BCA Green Mark certification scheme.

sections.label: Foreign worker supply and wages
sections.summary: Construction companies are badly affected by a drastic reduction in foreign worker supply, causing significant increases in daily wages and hiring costs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Many construction companies are badly affected due to the drastic reduction in the supply of foreign workers in the construction sector.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: As a result, there is a significant increase in the daily wages and other associated costs of hiring foreign workers.

sections.label: Rising costs and public housing
sections.summary: Rising construction costs may push property prices up as developers pass costs to buyers, raising questions about keeping public housing affordable.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: As the costs of construction increase, we can expect the property prices to rise further and developers will obviously pass the higher costs onto the buyers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: With more than 80% of our population staying in public housing, can we assure Singaporeans that public housing will be kept affordable, inclusive and liveable even with the rising cost of development?

sections.label: Construction Support Package measures
sections.summary: Support included a $1.36 billion Construction Support Package, levy waivers and rebates, wage subsidies, a lawsuit moratorium and developer cost-sharing.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We strived to ensure that no one segment of the value chain in the Built Environment sector bore a disproportionate share of the impact.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: So, to do this, we provided significant financial support, through a $1.36 billion Construction Support Package, waivers and rebates of the Foreign Worker Levy and wage subsidies under the Jobs Support Scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Through the COVID-19 (Temporary Measures) Act, we imposed a moratorium to protect the affected firms from contractual lawsuits and required developers to share in the costs of construction delays due to COVID-19.

sections.label: Construction demand recovery projection
sections.summary: Construction demand is projected to recover, with $23 billion to $28 billion in projects expected this year, up from $21 billion last year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We now project that construction demand will recover to some extent in the next few years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: This year, we expect $23 billion to $28 billion worth of projects to be awarded, up from $21 billion last year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: If needed, we will bring forward some of our planned public sector projects to help support the industry, as Mr Yip Hon Weng had suggested during the Budget debate.

sections.label: Growth and Transformation Scheme support
sections.summary: A new Growth and Transformation Scheme will support alliances of firms across the entire value chain to strengthen the Built Environment eco-system.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: And this pandemic has shown that we are only as strong as the weakest link in the chain.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We will, therefore, enhance Government support to further integrate and strengthen the entire value chain holistically, through a new Growth and Transformation Scheme, or GTS, which Deputy Prime Minister has announced in the Budget speech.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: First, unlike existing schemes that support individual firms, the GTS supports alliances of firms across the entire value chain, with the view of uplifting the entire Built Environment eco-system.

sections.label: Alliance business plans and productivity
sections.summary: Each alliance will develop a business plan of at least three years showing how it will increase productivity using Design for Manufacturing and Assembly and Integrated Digital Delivery.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Each alliance will develop a business plan of at least three years, showing how the alliance will increase productivity by using Design for Manufacturing and Assembly and the digital spine we call the Integrated Digital Delivery model.

sections.label: Removing Man-Year-Entitlement framework
sections.summary: MND announced in 2019 that the Man-Year-Entitlement framework will be removed and replaced with a system incentivising more productive off-site work.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: As announced at MND’s COS in 2019, we intend to remove the Man-Year-Entitlement (MYE) framework in the near future and replace it with a system that incentivises more productive off-site work.

sections.label: Keeping HDB flats affordable
sections.summary: New HDB flats are sold at subsidised prices with grants for first-timers, keeping estates inclusive; most non-mature estate first-timers pay mortgage within one-quarter of income.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: One important way we keep HDB estates inclusive is by keeping flats affordable, so that Singaporeans of different income levels can access home ownership and live in the same neighbourhoods.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: That is why we sell new HDB flats at subsidised prices and provide generous grants for first-timers buying both new and resale flats.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: For example, for most of the first-timer buyers in the non-mature estates, their monthly mortgage payment does not exceed one-quarter of their income.

sections.label: Public rental housing in prime areas
sections.summary: Bold action is needed so prime areas stay open and diverse, with public rental housing included so lower income households can live there.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We therefore need bold and decisive action to ensure that these prime areas of Singapore continue to reflect the openness and diversity of our society and allow Singaporeans from diverse backgrounds to live together and interact.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: That is why, even in these prime locations, we will strive to include public rental housing, so that lower income households can live in these estates too and be served by the facilities and services that they require.

sections.label: Recovering extra subsidies for prime flats
sections.summary: Additional subsidies could give owners more capital gains than other HDB flat owners, so a way may be needed to recover some extra subsidies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: These additional subsidies also cause difficulties, because they could lead to more capital gains for owners when they sell their flats on the open market, compared to other HDB flat owners.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Hence, for fairness, we may need a way to recover some of the extra subsidies provided for flats in very prime locations.

sections.label: Community Care Apartments pilot launch
sections.summary: Last month, with MOH colleagues, the first Community Care Apartments pilot was launched in Bukit Batok.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Last month, together with our colleagues from MOH, we launched the first pilot for the Community Care Apartments in Bukit Batok.

sections.label: Support for public rental households
sections.summary: HDB has a Home ownership Support Team for public rental households, and ComLink provides customised support to public rental families with children beyond housing needs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: For instance, we have a dedicated Home ownership Support Team in HDB to support public rental households who aspire to home ownership.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: And through ComLink, government agencies and community partners work together to provide customised and coordinated support to public rental families with children, beyond just tackling their housing needs.

sections.label: Combined HDB eligibility assessments
sections.summary: HDB's eligibility assessments for flats, loans and grants will be combined into a single service touchpoint.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: First, we will combine HDB’s eligibility assessments for flats, for loans, and for grants into a single service touchpoint.

sections.label: HDB Flat Eligibility letter
sections.summary: Outcomes will be sent to applicants in a single document called the HDB Flat Eligibility letter or HFE letter.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: The outcomes will be sent to applicants in a single document: the HDB Flat Eligibility letter or HFE letter.

sections.label: New HDB Flat Portal platform
sections.summary: A new digital platform in the HDB Flat Portal will guide new flat buyers from flat application to key collection.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Second, we will introduce a new digital platform in the HDB Flat Portal, to guide new flat buyers throughout their flat buying journey, from flat application to key collection.

sections.label: Extended loan-listing service
sections.summary: The loan-listing service in the HDB Flat Portal will be extended so home seekers can apply for housing loans from participating financial institutions through the portal.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Third, we will extend the loan-listing service in the HDB Flat Portal and enable home seekers to apply for housing loans from participating financial institutions, directly through the portal, instead of having to do so separately.

sections.label: Eastern and Central Corridors
sections.summary: The 18-km Eastern Corridor will link East Coast to Pasir Ris via Bedok Reservoir, and the 34-km Central Corridor will link Woodlands to the city centre.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The 18-km Eastern Corridor will link East Coast to Pasir Ris via Bedok Reservoir and the 34-km Central Corridor will link Woodlands in the North to the city centre.

sections.label: Coast-to-Coast Southern Trail
sections.summary: A 62-km Coast-to-Coast Southern Trail will be developed from Changi Beach to Tuas via Singapore Botanic Gardens.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In the South, we will develop a 62-km Coast-to-Coast Southern Trail from Changi Beach to Tuas via Singapore Botanic Gardens.

sections.label: Park connectors and City in Nature
sections.summary: Singaporeans can look forward to 500 km of park connectors by 2030, with over $315 million committed to City in Nature efforts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Overall, Singaporeans can look forward to 500 km of park connectors by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: At the same time, they will add to our island’s ecological connectivity and resilience.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We have committed over $315 million to these City in Nature efforts over the next few years.

sections.label: Long-Term Planning Review land use
sections.summary: MND and URA have embarked on the Long-Term Planning Review to guide future development, given Singapore's land area of just over 728 square kilometers.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: To guide future development, MND and URA have embarked on a review of our long-term land use plans.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: This exercise is known as the Long-Term Planning Review or the LTPR.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: This is crucial given our small land area of just over 728 square kilometers, which is less than 0.1% of the world’s largest country, Russia.

sections.label: First Concept Plan 1971
sections.summary: The first such plan, formerly the Concept Plan, was developed 50 years ago in 1971 and laid the foundation for the city's structure.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The first such plan, formerly known as the “Concept Plan”, was developed 50 years ago in 1971, and laid the foundation for our city's structure.

sections.label: CDB and SDI scheme applications
sections.summary: URA received nine outline applications under the CDB Incentive scheme, with six given in-principle approval, and three under the SDI scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: URA has received several proposals for both these schemes – nine outline applications under the CDB Incentive scheme of which six have been given in-principle approval.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Three outline applications were given in-principle approval under the SDI scheme.

sections.label: Engagement polls on future city
sections.summary: The engagement will kick off in April with polls on what Singaporeans want for the future city and why.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The engagement will kick off in April, with polls to get a pulse of what Singaporeans want for our future city and why they want it.

sections.label: Digitalising Built Environment AfA
sections.summary: The Digitalising Built Environment AfA was formed in June last year to accelerate digitalisation in the Built Environment sector.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: To accelerate digitalisation efforts in the Built Environment sector, we formed the Digitalising Built Environment AfA in June last year.

sections.label: Punggol Northshore smart district prototypes
sections.summary: HDB's first smart and sustainable district in Punggol Northshore will feature smart lighting, smart sockets, smart distribution boards and barrier-free parking.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: There are many more of such prototypes in the works – a testament to the ingenuity of our fellow Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We will scale up prototypes that prove to be effective.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: For example, in Punggol Northshore, HDB's very first "smart and sustainable district", we will get a glimpse of the neighbourhoods of the future.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Think sensor-controlled smart lighting in common areas, smart sockets and a smart distribution board in homes to help residents monitor energy consumption.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Residents will also enjoy a seamless parking experience with barrier-free entry and exit.

sections.label: OneService app user growth
sections.summary: The OneService community app has grown to over 340,000 users, up from less than 200,000 in 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: The one-stop OneService community app has also grown to over 340,000 users, up from less than 200,000 in 2019.

sections.label: Tampines municipal service delivery pilot
sections.summary: A new model of municipal service delivery will be piloted in Tampines town later this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: One such barrier is the delivery of municipal services along agency lines.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: That is why we are piloting a new model of municipal service delivery in Tampines town later this year.

sections.label: Chatbot prediction accuracy
sections.summary: The artificial intelligence-supported chatbot currently predicts case type and agency-in-charge with 80% accuracy based on residents' feedback.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: The chatbot is supported by artificial intelligence, which currently predicts with 80% accuracy, the case type and agency-in-charge based on residents' submitted feedback.

sections.label: Interface changes for action status
sections.summary: Changes to the interface will be implemented in the coming month to give residents a clearer understanding of agencies' action status.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: In the coming month, we will implement changes to the interface to provide residents a clearer understanding on the status of actions undertaken by agencies.

sections.label: Help Neighbour feature launch
sections.summary: With MSF and AIC, a new Help Neighbour feature will be introduced in the second half of this year for residents to alert agencies to persons needing assistance.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: In partnership with MSF and the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC), we will introduce a new “Help Neighbour” feature in the second half of this year, which residents can use to alert agencies to persons in need of assistance.

sections.label: HDB repair and upgrading help
sections.summary: HDB can help with rectifications and share half of repair costs under the Goodwill Repair Assistance Scheme, and all HDB blocks get HIP II at 60 to 70 years old.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: When such cases occur, HDB can help to make rectifications, and share half of the repair costs through the Goodwill Repair Assistance Scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: We have also announced that all HDB blocks will receive a second round of subsidised upgrading under HIP II when they reach 60 to 70 years old.

sections.label: Lift access Housing Grant
sections.summary: As LUP costs can approach new flat costs, the Lift access Housing Grant helps residents with urgent mobility or medical needs move to flats with direct lift access.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: In some cases, the LUP cost might be almost the same as that of a new flat.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Therefore, while we continue exploring new technical methods to bring down LUP costs, we have also introduced the Lift access Housing Grant (LHG), which helps residents with urgent mobility or medical needs to move to another flat with direct lift access.

sections.label: HDB facade repair cost sharing
sections.summary: Where HDB building facades need repairs, the Government will assist Town Councils with 50% of the costs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Where repairs are required for HDB building facades, the Government will assist Town Councils with 50% of the costs.

sections.label: HDB retailer mobile apps
sections.summary: HDB launched two new mobile apps, RetailerLink and ShopperLink, to enable HDB retailers to connect with shoppers online.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: For example, HDB launched two new mobile apps, RetailerLink and ShopperLink to enable HDB retailers to connect with shoppers online.

sections.label: Predictive maintenance and Tampines pilot
sections.summary: Technology will be used for predictive maintenance, and a new municipal service delivery model will be piloted in Tampines town later this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: First, we will leverage technology for predictive maintenance work to spot issues and resolve them before they become a problem for residents.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: We will also pilot a new model of municipal service delivery in Tampines town later this year, one that would integrate services around residents' needs at the township level, rather than by agency and land boundaries.

sections.label: OneService and Help Neighbour features
sections.summary: A OneService Lite reporting trial in Chinese, a OneService Chatbot, and a Help Neighbour feature will be introduced.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: We will also be starting a trial for OneService Lite reporting in Chinese, which will bring convenience to residents who are more comfortable with Chinese.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: We will also launch the OneService Chatbot in the second half of this year, which will guide residents to provide feedback via WhatsApp and Telegram.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Third, we will also introduce a new "Help Neighbour" feature in the second half of this year, which residents can use to alert agencies to persons in need of assistance.

sections.label: COVID-19 support for HDB households
sections.summary: Households in 1- and 2-room HDB flats received an average of $3,400 per member from COVID-19 Budget measures, and about 47,000 got rent rebates from October to December 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Households living in 1- and 2-room HDB flats received an average of $3,400 per member from the COVID-19 Budget measures.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: About 47,000 such households benefited from three months of rent rebates from October to December 2020.

sections.label: Rental household rent savings
sections.summary: About 350 rental households have benefited so far, with median rent savings of about $150 per month.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: About 350 rental households have benefited so far, with median rent savings of about $150 per month.

sections.label: Rental households moving into homes
sections.summary: In the past five years, about 4,600 rental households have moved into their own homes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: In the past five years, about 4,600 rental households have moved into their own homes.

sections.label: 3-room rental flats for large families
sections.summary: MND and HDB will work with MSF under ComLink to offer 3-room rental flats to large families with children, on a case-by-case basis.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: To better support large families staying in public rental flats, MND and HDB will also work with MSF under ComLink to offer 3-room rental flats to large families with children, on a case-by-case basis.

sections.label: Partitions in 1-room rental flats
sections.summary: HDB has been building new 1-room rental flats with partitions, including some with internal doors, and there are currently 705 such flats with pre-installed partitions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: To provide more privacy, HDB has been building new 1-room rental flats with partitions, including some that have internal doors to separate the sleeping areas.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: There are currently 705 such rental flats with pre-installed partitions.

sections.label: Singles applying under JSS
sections.summary: HDB will pilot a new model allowing singles applying under the JSS to apply individually, without having to find a flatmate first.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: To provide an additional option to singles who apply under the JSS, HDB will pilot a new model which will allow them to apply individually, without having to find a flatmate first.

sections.label: CCAs and flat applications
sections.summary: Members asked about CCAs and future plans; 706 applicants applied for 169 units.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Mr Xie Yao Quan and Mr Henry Kwek Hian Chuan spoke about the CCAs and asked about our future plans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: We received a very positive response for these flats, with 706 applicants applying for 169 units.

sections.label: 3-room rental flats for large families
sections.summary: MND and HDB will work with ComLink to offer 3-room rental flats to large families case-by-case.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: To better support large families living in public rental flats, MND and HDB will work with Community Link (or ComLink), which is an MSF initiative, to offer 3-room rental flats to large families on a case-by-case basis.

sections.label: ComLink support for rental families
sections.summary: All public rental flat families with small children will receive holistic ComLink support for stability, self-reliance and social mobility.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: At the same time, all public rental flat families with small children will receive holistic support under ComLink to enable them to achieve stability, self-reliance and social mobility.

sections.label: Housing grants and rent stability
sections.summary: Housing grants support first-time buyers, and HDB will not raise rent for new flat down-payers during their rental stay.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Indeed, owning a home is a milestone that brings pride and joy for them.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: We will continue supporting them to realise this aspiration, by providing various housing grants for first-time flat buyers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: For those who make a down payment for a new flat, HDB will not increase their rent for the rest of their stay in rental housing.

sections.label: ITM construction sector outcomes
sections.summary: The 2017 ITM rallied the construction sector; over 40% of buildings are greened and energy use and productivity improved.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: The ITM was launched in 2017 to rally the construction sector around the shared goal of developing future-ready capabilities that would transform our Built Environment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: We have greened over 40% of our buildings.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: The overall energy use intensity of our buildings has improved by 10% over the past decade.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: At the worksite, we have seen a 7% improvement in productivity since 2017.

sections.label: DfMA adoption increase
sections.summary: DfMA adoption doubled over three years, from 19% in 2017 to 39% in 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: DfMA adoption has doubled over the last three years, from 19% in 2017 to 39% in 2020.

sections.label: Minimum energy performance requirements
sections.summary: Revised requirements will make all new buildings 50% more energy-efficient than the 2005 baseline, applying to new developments from Q4 this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: Last year, we announced that we would raise minimum energy performance requirements for new buildings and existing buildings that undergo major retrofitting.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: Under these revised requirements, all new buildings will be 50% more energy-efficient than the 2005 baseline.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: This is equivalent to our current Green Mark Platinum standard.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: These requirements will apply to new developments submitted for planning approval from the fourth quarter of this year.

sections.label: DfMA minimum B-score
sections.summary: Minimum B-score was raised for large residential non-landed developments from December 2019 and will rise for commercial, institutional and industrial developments from April 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: To drive DfMA adoption, we have raised the minimum B-score for large residential, non-landed developments with GFA of at least 25,000 sqm from December 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: We will raise the minimum B-score for large commercial, institutional and industrial developments with GFA of at least 25,000 sqm next year, starting from April 2022.

sections.label: CPCF funding extension
sections.summary: Over 10,000 firms were supported and close to two-thirds of about $850 million disbursed, and the CPCF will be extended till March 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: Since its launch in 2010, we have supported over 10,000 firms and disbursed close to two-thirds of the approximately $850 million we have been allocated in funding.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: To support our firms, especially our SMEs, we will extend the CPCF by another year till March 2022.

sections.label: Construction jobs and training opportunities
sections.summary: As at end 2020, there were about 7,500 jobs and training opportunities in the construction industry under the SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: As at end 2020, there were about 7,500 jobs and training opportunities in the construction industry under the SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package.

sections.label: Training 80,000 professionals
sections.summary: The aim is to train 80,000 professionals in the key transformation areas under the ITM by 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: Through these collective efforts, we aim to train 80,000 professionals in the key transformation areas under the ITM by 2025.

sections.label: GTS Alliance-based scheme
sections.summary: Firms keen to participate in the GTS, an Alliance-based scheme, can approach BCA or the BuildSG office to transform together.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We set it up a few years ago to provide more integrated support for our firms and our workforce who would like to go on to this transformation journey.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: So, certainly, in relation to the GPC Chairman's question, if there are firms that are keen to participate in the GTS – and remember that the GTS is not a firm-based scheme but an Alliance-based scheme from developer to consultant to builder and subcontractors, the whole eco-system that they work with to make their projects come true – if they can transform together, then approach BCA, approach the BuildSG office and we will work with them.

sections.label: Temporary permission, rental relief support
sections.summary: URA uses a risk-based approach for temporary permission length, while MOF, property tax rebates and MinLaw support firms on land costs and leases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: And in considering the length of the temporary permission to be granted, URA looks at it from a risk-based approach based on the potential impact of the proposal on surrounding developments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: So, for cases involving a TDL, URA typically gives businesses options to decide on the length of the TDL or the temporary permission that they require which typically varies from one to five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: But on a holistic basis, when it comes to support for firms in relation to land costs and rental, MOF had rolled out a rental relief framework for SMEs under COTMA, which is the COVID-19 (Temporary Measures) Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: There was a property tax rebate available to qualifying firms and, under the Re-align Framework by MinLaw, small and micro businesses may re-negotiate leases for non-residential properties with a term of five years or less.

sections.label: MSCP commercial use proposals
sections.summary: URA would consider specific MSCP proposals, weighing loading factor, water provision and impact on residents of commercial use.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: In the case of MSCPs, for instance, we may have to look at loading factor, provision of water and also, very importantly, because the space may not have been originally intended for commercial purposes, what would be the impact to residents in terms of people moving in and out and so forth?

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: So, I think we would be prepared to look at specific proposals if the Member has something to share or a plan to share.

sections.label: Spalling concrete repair assistance
sections.summary: Beyond the goodwill repair assistance scheme, HDB researches better repair methods and plans for HIP2, and will visit the units mentioned.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: When it comes to spalling concrete, we help our residents beyond the goodwill repair assistance scheme, which I should also add households can benefit from more than once.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: We are also assisting by researching into better repair methods so as to be able to advise the contractors accordingly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: I have also shared more comprehensive plans are being looked at but that would be further down the line because that would be for our HIP2 and more details will be shared closer to commencement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: However, we do take the Member's feedback very seriously and I will come and visit the units that you have mentioned, together with HDB, to ensure that residents' concerns are being addressed.

sections.label: Built Environment Living Lab Framework
sections.summary: The Living Lab Framework, launched in September last year, facilitates test bedding in government living labs like Punggol town and Jurong Lake District.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: In September last year, we launched the Built Environment Living Laboratory Framework or Living Lab Framework to facilitate the test bedding of innovative proposals in "government living labs", such as designated areas within Punggol town and the Jurong Lake District.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: The Living Lab Framework helps to strengthen partnerships between the public and private sector, and creates opportunities to harness and trial new, emerging technologies to jointly develop cities for tomorrow.

sections.label: Parenthood Provisional Housing Scheme
sections.summary: PPHS is another means by which HDB rents out flats, allowing young couples privacy and to set up their family.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: But the other means through which HDB rents out flats is the Parenthood Provisional Housing Scheme (PPHS).

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: It is a scheme that allows young couples who desire some privacy and to be able to set up their family.

sections.label: PPHS supply from SERS flats
sections.summary: Flats from SERS sites are held back and used for PPHS, and HDB will look at ways to increase PPHS supply amid COVID-19 construction delays.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: From flats that have been SERS-ed, we hold back the redevelopment because it is not needed immediately, and we use those flats in order to provide the PPHS option.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: And because there is great interest in PPHS flats, particularly during this period when there is COVID-19 and there are delays in construction, HDB will look at ways to increase PPHS supply.

sections.label: EIP impact and support
sections.summary: The EIP can legitimately impact some households, so recent affected resales and price points are reviewed and support is provided in extenuating circumstances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Having said that, we are very mindful that in certain instances, the EIP can legitimately impact some households.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We look at the recent resales that have been similarly affected by EIP in the neighbourhood, and look at the price points.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We look at a range of considerations and in extenuating circumstances, we provide support.

sections.label: Flat pricing based on affordability
sections.summary: Flats are priced on affordability, not land or construction costs, using household income share and income-to-price index.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: It does not look at land costs or construction costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: It prices flats based on affordability – looking at, for example, the percentage of household income that our typical households have to fork out to pay for their flats, as well as the household income to price index, to see how many years of income it typically takes to pay for a flat.
